title: Net 15 payment
text: Client shall pay each undisputed invoice within fifteen (15) days of receipt.
notes: Short payment window protects the freelancer's cash flow.

title: Late fee on overdue invoices
text: Invoices not paid within thirty (30) days of receipt shall accrue a late fee of 1.5% per month on the unpaid balance.
notes: Gives the client a reason to pay on time.

title: Deposit before work begins
text: Client shall pay a non-refundable deposit of fifty percent (50%) of the project fee before Contractor begins work.
notes: Shares the risk of non-payment up front.

title: Milestone payments
text: Fees are payable in installments upon completion of each milestone listed in Schedule A, within fifteen (15) days of the milestone invoice.
notes: Payment tracks delivered work instead of arriving only at the end.

title: Kill fee on cancellation
text: If Client cancels the project for convenience, Client shall pay for all work performed to date plus a cancellation fee of twenty-five percent (25%) of the remaining fees.
notes: Compensates the freelancer for reserved time.

title: Reimbursed expenses
text: Client shall reimburse Contractor for reasonable pre-approved expenses within fifteen (15) days of receiving receipts.
notes: Contractor is not out of pocket for project costs.

title: Limited invoice disputes
text: Client may dispute an invoice only in writing, within ten (10) days of receipt, stating the specific reason, and shall pay the undisputed portion on time.
notes: Stops open-ended payment holds.

title: Net 60 payment
text: Client shall pay invoices within sixty (60) days of receipt.
notes: A two-month wait strains a freelancer's cash flow.

title: Pay when paid
text: Client shall pay Contractor only after Client has received payment from its own customer for the related project.
notes: Shifts the end customer's credit risk to the freelancer.

title: Payment at client's discretion
text: Client may withhold payment for any deliverable it considers unsatisfactory, in its sole discretion.
notes: Lets the client avoid paying without a stated reason.

title: Payment within a reasonable time
text: Client shall pay undisputed invoices within a reasonable time after receipt.
notes: No deadline means no enforceable due date.

title: No expense reimbursement
text: All expenses incurred in performing the Services are the sole responsibility of Contractor.
notes: Travel, software, and materials come out of the fee.

title: Fee reduction for delay
text: Client may reduce the fee by ten percent (10%) for each week any deliverable is late, regardless of cause.
notes: Penalizes delays the client itself may cause.

title: Liability capped at fees paid
text: Each party's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid to Contractor in the twelve (12) months before the claim.
notes: Caps the worst-case loss at a known amount.

title: No consequential damages
text: Neither party shall be liable for any indirect, incidental, consequential, or punitive damages, including lost profits.
notes: Excludes open-ended business losses.

title: Mutual limitation
text: The limitations of liability in this Section apply equally to both parties.
notes: Both sides carry the same risk.

title: Disclaimer of implied warranties
text: Except as expressly stated in this Agreement, the deliverables are provided as is, and Contractor disclaims all implied warranties, including merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose.
notes: Limits promises to what was actually agreed.

title: Short warranty period
text: Contractor warrants that the deliverables will materially conform to the specifications for thirty (30) days after delivery; Client's sole remedy is correction of the nonconformity.
notes: A defined, limited fix-it obligation.

title: Liability capped at the project fee
text: Contractor's aggregate liability for all claims arising from this Agreement is limited to the total fees payable under the applicable Statement of Work.
notes: Exposure never exceeds the job's value.

title: Claims deadline
text: Any claim arising under this Agreement must be brought within one (1) year after the cause of action arises.
notes: Old claims can't resurface years later.

title: Unlimited contractor liability
text: Contractor shall be liable for any and all damages arising from the Services, without limitation as to amount or type.
notes: Exposure can exceed many times the fee.

title: One-sided cap
text: Client's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed one hundred dollars ($100). No limit applies to Contractor's liability.
notes: Only the client is protected.

title: Liability for consequential damages
text: Contractor shall be liable for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, including Client's lost profits and lost business opportunities.
notes: Lost profits can dwarf the fee.

title: Unlimited warranty
text: Contractor warrants that the deliverables will be error-free and fit for any purpose Client intends, for the life of the deliverables.
notes: An open-ended promise no software can meet.

title: Liability regardless of fault
text: Contractor is responsible for any loss relating to the project, whether or not caused by Contractor.
notes: Makes the freelancer an insurer for the client.

title: Punitive damages
text: Contractor shall be liable for punitive and exemplary damages in addition to actual damages.
notes: Adds penalties beyond actual harm.

title: Mutual indemnification
text: Each party shall indemnify the other against third-party claims to the extent caused by its own negligence or willful misconduct.
notes: Each side covers only its own fault.

title: Indemnity limited to IP infringement
text: Contractor shall indemnify Client only against third-party claims that original material created by Contractor infringes a copyright.
notes: A narrow, insurable obligation.

title: Client indemnifies for its materials
text: Client shall indemnify Contractor against claims arising from materials, data, or instructions supplied by Client.
notes: Freelancer is not liable for the client's content.

title: Indemnity subject to the cap
text: Any indemnification obligation of Contractor is subject to the limitation of liability in Section 8.
notes: Indemnity can't bypass the liability cap.

title: Notice and control of defense
text: The indemnified party shall give prompt written notice of a claim and allow the indemnifying party to control its defense and settlement.
notes: Prevents surprise bills for claims handled badly.

title: Exclusion for client modifications
text: Contractor has no indemnity obligation for claims caused by Client's modification of the deliverables or their combination with other products.
notes: Freelancer isn't liable for what the client changed.

title: One-way indemnification
text: Contractor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Client from any and all claims, losses, and expenses arising from or relating to this Agreement.
notes: Covers claims the freelancer didn't cause.

title: Indemnity regardless of fault
text: Contractor shall indemnify Client against all claims related to the Services, regardless of fault.
notes: Even the client's own mistakes are on the freelancer.

title: Uncapped indemnity
text: Contractor's indemnification obligations are not subject to any limitation of liability.
notes: Unlimited exposure through the back door.

title: Defense costs at client's choice
text: Contractor shall pay all attorneys' fees of counsel chosen by Client in defending any claim related to the deliverables.
notes: Client controls the spending, freelancer pays.

title: Indemnity for client's materials
text: Contractor shall indemnify Client against claims arising from any content incorporated into the deliverables, including content supplied by Client.
notes: Freelancer is liable for the client's own content.

title: Indemnity survives forever
text: Contractor's indemnification obligations survive termination of this Agreement indefinitely.
notes: Exposure never ends.

title: Indemnity includes Client's affiliates
text: Contractor shall indemnify Client and all of its affiliates, officers, employees, customers, and agents against any claim relating to the Services.
notes: Extends the obligation to an open-ended group.

title: Ownership on full payment
text: Ownership of the deliverables transfers to Client upon Contractor's receipt of full payment.
notes: Freelancer keeps leverage until paid.

title: Contractor keeps pre-existing IP
text: Contractor retains all rights in its pre-existing tools, code, libraries, and know-how, and grants Client a non-exclusive license to use them as part of the deliverables.
notes: Reusable tools stay with the freelancer.

title: Portfolio rights
text: Contractor may display the deliverables in its portfolio and marketing materials after public release, unless Client objects in writing for confidentiality reasons.
notes: Freelancer can show the work to win more.

title: License instead of assignment
text: Contractor grants Client a perpetual, non-exclusive license to use the deliverables for Client's internal business purposes; Contractor retains ownership.
notes: Freelancer can reuse and resell the work.

title: Assignment limited to final deliverables
text: Only the final deliverables accepted by Client are assigned; drafts, concepts, and unused materials remain Contractor's property.
notes: Unused ideas stay with the freelancer.

title: Attribution
text: Client shall credit Contractor as the creator of the deliverables in any public use, where customary.
notes: Builds the freelancer's reputation.

title: Assignment upon creation
text: All work product is the sole property of Client upon creation, whether or not Client has paid for it.
notes: The client owns the work even if it never pays.

title: Assignment of pre-existing IP
text: Contractor assigns to Client all rights in any materials used in the Services, including Contractor's pre-existing tools and code.
notes: Freelancer loses tools it built before this job.

title: Work made for hire of everything
text: All work performed by Contractor during the term, whether or not related to the project, is a work made for hire owned by Client.
notes: Captures unrelated side work.

title: No portfolio use
text: Contractor shall not display, reference, or describe the deliverables or the project in any portfolio or marketing material.
notes: Freelancer can't show the work to win clients.

title: Waiver of moral rights
text: Contractor irrevocably waives all moral rights and rights of attribution in the deliverables.
notes: Removes credit and integrity rights.

title: Future ideas assigned
text: Contractor assigns to Client all ideas and inventions conceived during the term and for one (1) year afterward that relate to Client's business.
notes: Reaches ideas after the job ends.

title: Power of attorney
text: Contractor appoints Client as its attorney-in-fact to execute any documents needed to perfect Client's ownership of the deliverables.
notes: Client can sign IP documents in the freelancer's name.

title: Payment for work done on termination
text: Upon termination for any reason, Client shall pay Contractor for all Services performed through the termination date.
notes: Freelancer is paid for completed work.

title: Mutual notice period
text: Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience with thirty (30) days' written notice.
notes: Both sides get the same exit terms.

title: Cure period for breach
text: A party may terminate for breach only if the breach remains uncured thirty (30) days after written notice describing it.
notes: A chance to fix problems before losing the contract.

title: Contractor may terminate for non-payment
text: Contractor may suspend work or terminate if any invoice remains unpaid fifteen (15) days after its due date.
notes: Freelancer isn't forced to keep working unpaid.

title: Termination fee
text: If Client terminates for convenience, Client shall pay a termination fee of twenty percent (20%) of the remaining contract value.
notes: Compensates for lost reserved time.

title: Return of materials both ways
text: Upon termination, each party shall return or destroy the other's confidential materials within thirty (30) days.
notes: Clean, mutual wrap-up.

title: Payment for committed costs
text: Upon termination, Client shall reimburse non-cancellable expenses Contractor incurred before the termination date.
notes: Covers costs already committed.

title: Termination at will by client only
text: Client may terminate this Agreement at any time, for any reason or no reason, without notice; Contractor may terminate only for Client's material breach.
notes: Only the client can walk away freely.

title: No payment for work in progress
text: Upon termination, Client owes no payment for work in progress or deliverables not yet accepted.
notes: Unfinished work goes unpaid.

title: Long notice for contractor only
text: Contractor must give one hundred twenty (120) days' written notice to terminate; Client may terminate immediately.
notes: Locks the freelancer in, not the client.

title: Forfeiture of fees on termination
text: If this Agreement is terminated for any reason, all unpaid fees are forfeited.
notes: Termination becomes a way to avoid paying.

title: Refund of fees on termination
text: Upon termination, Contractor shall refund all fees paid for deliverables not yet accepted.
notes: Claws back pay for work already done.

title: Automatic renewal
text: This Agreement renews automatically for successive one-year terms unless Contractor gives notice at least ninety (90) days before the renewal date.
notes: Easy to miss the window and get locked in.

title: No non-compete
text: Nothing in this Agreement restricts Contractor from providing services to other clients, including clients in Client's industry.
notes: Freelancer can keep working for others.

title: Narrow non-solicitation
text: During the term and for six (6) months after, Contractor shall not directly solicit Client's employees whom Contractor worked with on the project.
notes: Short and limited to people the freelancer met.

title: Mutual non-solicitation
text: Neither party shall solicit the other's employees for six (6) months after this Agreement ends.
notes: Protects both sides equally.

title: Non-compete limited to named competitors
text: For three (3) months after termination, Contractor shall not provide the same services to the two competitors named in Schedule B.
notes: Narrow, specific, and short.

title: Paid exclusivity
text: If Client requires exclusivity, Client shall pay an exclusivity fee equal to twenty percent (20%) of the monthly fee for each month of exclusivity.
notes: The freelancer is paid for lost work.

title: Restriction ends with the project
text: Any restriction on Contractor's work for competitors ends on completion of the project.
notes: No restriction after the job.

title: Worldwide multi-year non-compete
text: For three (3) years after termination, Contractor shall not provide services to any business anywhere in the world that competes with Client.
notes: Could block the freelancer's whole field.

title: Exclusivity without pay
text: During the term, Contractor shall work exclusively for Client and shall not accept any other engagement.
notes: Bars other income at no extra pay.

title: Non-solicitation of all customers
text: For two (2) years after termination, Contractor shall not accept work from any customer or prospective customer of Client, whether or not Contractor solicited them.
notes: Blocks clients who come to the freelancer.

title: Broad industry restriction
text: Contractor shall not perform any services in Client's industry for any person during the term and for one (1) year afterward.
notes: Covers the freelancer's entire market.

title: Liquidated damages for competition
text: If Contractor breaches the non-competition covenant, Contractor shall pay Client liquidated damages of fifty thousand dollars ($50,000).
notes: A fixed penalty larger than most projects.

title: Non-compete regardless of termination reason
text: The non-competition covenant applies even if Client terminates this Agreement without cause.
notes: Client can end the work and still restrict the freelancer.

title: No-hire of client's contractors
text: Contractor shall not work alongside or partner with any other contractor of Client for two (2) years.
notes: Limits future collaborations.

title: Mutual confidentiality
text: Each party shall keep the other's confidential information secret and use it only to perform this Agreement.
notes: Both sides protect each other.

title: Standard exclusions
text: Confidential information does not include information that is public, already known to the recipient, independently developed, or received lawfully from a third party.
notes: Common knowledge can't become a secret.

title: Limited duration
text: Confidentiality obligations last for three (3) years after this Agreement ends, except for trade secrets, which last as long as they remain trade secrets.
notes: A defined end date.

title: Disclosure required by law
text: The recipient may disclose confidential information when required by law or court order, after giving prompt notice where legally allowed.
notes: No breach for obeying a subpoena.

title: General skills retained
text: Contractor may use the general skills, knowledge, and experience gained during the project.
notes: Freelancer keeps what it learned.

title: Marking requirement
text: Information is confidential only if marked confidential or identified as confidential in writing within ten (10) days of disclosure.
notes: Clear what must be protected.

title: One-way confidentiality
text: Contractor shall keep confidential all information about Client; Client has no confidentiality obligation to Contractor.
notes: Freelancer's own information is unprotected.

title: Perpetual confidentiality
text: Contractor's confidentiality obligations continue forever.
notes: An obligation that never ends.

title: Everything is confidential
text: All information Contractor receives or learns in any way during the term, whether or not marked, is confidential.
notes: Even public information becomes a breach risk.

title: No legal-disclosure exception
text: Contractor shall not disclose confidential information for any reason, including under subpoena, without Client's prior written consent.
notes: Forces a choice between court and contract.

title: Confidentiality of the agreement's existence
text: Contractor shall not disclose that it has worked for Client or that this Agreement exists.
notes: Freelancer can't name the client at all.

title: Return of all work notes
text: Upon request, Contractor shall deliver to Client all notes, drafts, and working files, including Contractor's general know-how documents.
notes: Takes the freelancer's own reference material.

title: Penalty for any disclosure
text: Any disclosure of confidential information, however minor, entitles Client to liquidated damages of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000).
notes: A fixed penalty unrelated to actual harm.

title: Contractor's home law
text: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the state where Contractor resides.
notes: Freelancer knows the rules that apply.

title: Neutral venue
text: Disputes shall be resolved in the courts of a mutually agreed county, or by video-conference mediation before any lawsuit.
notes: Neither side gets a travel advantage.

title: Small claims available
text: Either party may bring a claim in small claims court for disputes within that court's limit.
notes: A cheap option for unpaid invoices.

title: Mediation first
text: Before filing suit, the parties shall try in good faith to resolve any dispute through non-binding mediation, sharing its cost equally.
notes: Cheaper than going straight to court.

title: Prevailing party fees
text: The prevailing party in any action to enforce this Agreement may recover reasonable attorneys' fees.
notes: Makes collecting small debts worth it.

title: Remote proceedings
text: Any arbitration hearing shall be held by video conference unless both parties agree otherwise.
notes: No costly travel to the client's city.

title: Client's home forum
text: Any dispute shall be brought exclusively in the courts of Client's home county, and Contractor submits to that jurisdiction.
notes: Freelancer must travel to sue or defend.

title: Mandatory arbitration paid by contractor
text: All disputes shall be resolved by binding arbitration in Client's city, with all arbitration fees paid by Contractor.
notes: Costly enough to deter any claim.

title: Waiver of jury and class actions
text: Contractor waives any right to a jury trial and to participate in any class or collective action.
notes: Removes common ways to enforce rights.

title: Foreign governing law
text: This Agreement is governed by the laws of a foreign country where Client is incorporated.
notes: Unfamiliar law and expensive advice.

title: Client recovers fees only
text: Client may recover its attorneys' fees in any dispute; Contractor may not.
notes: Only one side can recover costs.

title: Shortened time to sue
text: Contractor must bring any claim within ninety (90) days after it arises, or the claim is waived.
notes: Unpaid invoices can expire quickly.

title: Client chooses forum later
text: Client may choose the forum for any dispute at the time the dispute arises.
notes: Freelancer can't predict where it will be sued.
